description: Run by the renovate repo's workflow (the global config, and default.json for the shared settings). Every update is a PR, nothing automerges: applies are deliberate. PRs are rebased whenever master moves on, so a clusters plan always runs against current master.

customManagers.description: Versions with a `# renovate: datasource=... depName=...` comment on the line above (lint.yml, the roles' defaults)
Terraform variables with a `# renovate:` comment above the block (talos_version, kubernetes_version)

packageRules.description: The Terraform CLI (required_version in every root, lint.yml and clusters.yml) follows Arch Linux's package, the workstation's version. Repology gives Arch's version with its pkgrel (1.15.9-1) and no release dates: Arch's packaging is the wait.
prBodyNotes: Update the workstation from Arch first. Merging this runs the clusters workflow with it (a no-op apply).

packageRules.description: Talos and Kubernetes: one minor version at a time, each applied when merged
prBodyNotes: Upgrades the cluster when merged (the clusters workflow applies it, one node at a time): read the plan on this PR first. [tools-bin's PR](https://github.com/HiredNoobs/tools-bin/pulls?q=is%3Apr+{{{depName}}}) bumps talosctl/kubectl in `context-setup`: merge it once this is applied (the management VMs get them with `mgmt.yml`). For Kubernetes, bump `KUBERNETES_VERSION` (and the schemas commit) in iac-k8s's lint.yml. Check the Talos support matrix first.
15.0 is the LTS line (until July 2027): a new major leaves it. Check the binary's .asc against the Forgejo release key, then `forgejo.yml`.

packageRules.description: Leaving the LTS line is a decision: a new major only gets a PR once ticked in the Dependency Dashboard
Vault itself (the vault role's pin), not the Terraform provider of the same name
prBodyNotes: Check the zip's SHA256SUMS signature against HashiCorp's key, take a Raft snapshot, then `vault.yml`. [tools-bin's PR](https://github.com/HiredNoobs/tools-bin/pulls?q=is%3Apr+hashicorp%2Fvault) bumps the client (`VAULT_VERSION` in `context-setup`): merge it with this one, the management VMs get it with `mgmt.yml`.

packageRules.description: Checks before and after merging and applying (prBodyNotes add up across rules)
prBodyNotes: Before (each node is drained and rebooted): Grafana Storage → Longhorn with no degraded volumes and every node schedulable (a drain waits on a volume's last healthy copy), Control plane → etcd healthy, then `deployment longhorn_backup`. After: `kubectl get nodes -o wide` on the new version, Longhorn volumes healthy again, `deployment status falco` with a pod on every node, `flux get kustomizations -A` Ready.
After: `kubectl get nodes -o wide` on the new version, Grafana Control plane → API server and etcd healthy, `flux get kustomizations -A` Ready, KubeDeprecatedAPIUsed quiet.

After `forgejo.yml`: the new version in Forgejo's footer, `flux get sources git -A` and `flux get kustomizations -A` Ready (Flux pulls iac-k8s from Forgejo), a lint run passes (the runner reconnects), the push mirrors to GitHub still sync.
After `forgejo-runner.yml`: a lint run on any PR is picked up and passes.

After `vault.yml`: unseal it (`vault-unseal.yml`), `vault status` unsealed, `vsecret ls`, `kubectl get externalsecrets -A` still SecretSynced, Grafana Services → Hashicorp Vault; VaultSealed and VaultDown quiet.
A provider bump should change nothing: label this PR and read the clusters plan. CI never plans the gitops and vault roots, run `terraform plan` in those by hand before merging.
Applied with `monitoring.yml` (the VMs) and `./build.sh proxmox` (the Proxmox hosts). After: Grafana Hosts → Node Exporter Full fills for every host, TargetDown quiet.
Applied with `monitoring.yml`. After: Grafana Monitoring → Log pipeline still has every VM's journal, VectorSendFailing quiet.
